prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this system

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the cleanest example on the shortlist of what I mean by putting the discovery first: a sharp, falsifiable prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, 2011) that nature then confirmed in 2018 with correlated insulators and superconductivity at the predicted twist angle. It was not a case of thinking alone; the clue came from the experiment. The result has been reproduced by many independent groups in a few years, has spawned a whole family of moire platforms, and gives a tunable knob for strongly correlated matter that was not available before. It is also timely rather than premature, since the core phenomenology is secure even though the pairing mechanism is not. Seven of eight members named the same trio of Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Bistritzer, and four of us placed it first, so the configuration is both scientifically defensible and the one with the least friction.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution and maturity together. The credited-name limit forces us to leave out Eva Andrei, whose STM work on flat bands in twisted layers is an early experimental strand, and the first-author experimentalists of the 2018 papers, as well as Dean, Kim and others on hBN moire devices. The origin of the superconductivity is still open, and sample-to-sample twist-angle disorder limits how sharply the experimental claims can be stated. If the committee judges that the discovery is the platform rather than a settled explanation, one could argue that waiting a few more years would let the physics clarify who really opened the field.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B033 first but would give the third seat to Eva Andrei rather than Bistritzer, and says the choice between them is arguable and he defers to colleagues.
responses.response: I take the Andrei claim seriously and said so in my own opening, but I come down on Bistritzer. The prize citation is about a prediction that was then tested, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald paper is the only source of the magic-angle idea; without it the 2018 observations at the particular twist angle would not have been read as flat-band physics. Andrei's STM work established flat-band-like features and Van Hove singularities in twisted layers, which is a valuable but earlier and more general observation. I would be uncomfortable with a prize that drops the theory half of a theory-experiment pair. I would, however, accept that this is the weakest part of the configuration.

responses.point: Mehlig calls B033 a clean mechanism: prediction by Bistritzer and MacDonald, then the 2018 discovery by Jarillo-Herrero's group, with Andrei and the Dean/Kim contributions real but secondary to this one-two punch.
responses.response: I agree with the structure, and with the point that a theory-plus-experiment trio is the natural shape. Where I would qualify it is the word secondary. The Dean and Kim work on hBN moire superlattices was a genuinely independent line that shaped the field, and I do not want us to write a citation that suggests the field began only in 2018. That is why I prefer a citation naming the prediction and the discovery of correlated and superconducting states specifically, and not the whole moire field.

responses.point: Pearce ranks IceCube (B024) first on the strength of a patient instrument achievement that opened a new observational window, and ranks B033 third, calling it timely but somewhat early with the pairing mechanism unsettled.
responses.response: I share the appetite for a new window on the universe and I ranked IceCube fourth for that reason. My difficulty is attribution: the supplied credit is a single name for a collaboration of hundreds, and a prize to Halzen alone would be a narrow reading of who made the discovery. On the maturity point I disagree about how much the open pairing mechanism should weigh. The discovery being honoured is the observation of correlated and superconducting phases at the magic angle, which is secure, not a complete theory of why. We have given Nobel prizes where the mechanism was incomplete, including high-temperature superconductivity itself.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks optical lattice clocks (B026) first and topological insulators (B009) third, noting that the 2016 topological-phase prize is related but that B009 is a distinct step.
responses.response: I find B026 compelling on measurement grounds and kept it among my alternatives. My hesitation is whether the clock case is a single discovery or the continuation of a line already honoured in 2005 and 2012, and the redefinition of the second has not happened yet. On B009, I agree with her that the 2016 overlap is manageable, since that prize was about topological phase transitions and Thouless-style invariants in different systems, but I would not want to see it ahead of B033 until the Mele versus Hasan question has a defensible answer.

uncertainties: Whether the third seat should go to Bistritzer or to Eva Andrei, and whether the committee would accept leaving out the first-author experimentalists of the 2018 papers.
Whether recognising the platform before the pairing mechanism is understood will look premature in hindsight.
My recollection of priority details for the 2018 experiments and the earlier STM work is from memory and has not been verified here.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My research is in string theory and cosmology, with no collaboration or institutional tie to the moire-materials, topological or atomic-physics candidates. I trained with David Gross, but he is not a candidate on this shortlist. As Secretary I should be careful that my procedural role does not weigh in favour of any candidate.
